topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the cancer lecture series, and presents the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Concepts of Cancer Causation, Risk Factors, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and examine the relative contributions of intrinsic random mutations, environmental exposures, and epidemiological patterns to cancer risk.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biological and molecular mechanisms of carcinogenesis, encompassing oncogenic pathogens, direct and metabolically activated chemical and physical mutagens, tumor promoters, and host developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Determining and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the analytical, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes by summarizing the complexities of environmental carcinogenesis and weighing the practical risk-benefit decisions involved in daily life.
